runtime_prompt_en: A photographic live-performance frame of a small live band making music together on a low, intimate club stage. The reference-guided lead musician plays electric guitar at front-left, with a bassist half a pace behind at center and a drummer at the open right edge. The lead gives the drummer a small downward head cue; the drummer looks directly toward that cue as the near-hand drumstick tip strikes the snare skin. The bassist follows the same exchange while holding the groove. Their shared attention and quiet physical concentration make the groove feel inhabited. The lead has a softly tapered oval face, dark rounded almond eyes, gently arched straight brows, a small softly rounded nose, and softly full natural pink lips; a chin-length straight dark bob with a loose central part and fine wispy strands over the forehead. For this lead, use the supplied image for visible face and hair guidance. Frame the complete trio and their equipment in a shallow horizontal arrangement. The lead fills most of the vertical frame, with both shoes and usable floor margin visible. The camera looks across the stage from a modestly elevated front-left three-quarter position, showing the guitar face, the snare head, and the right-side profile of the drummer's seat in the same sharp plane. The lead is the largest figure, wearing a plain dark sleeveless top and charcoal trousers, with a calm, vivid expression and an easy grounded stance. A broad shoulder strap carries the guitar. The lead's left fingertips visibly press the strings onto the fretboard, with the left thumb behind the neck; the right thumb and forefinger hold a small pale pick whose tip meets the strings over the bridge pickup. Both hands connect naturally through relaxed wrists and elbows to the same shoulders. The whole guitar, neck and headstock are inside the frame; both shoes stand separately on the stage. Place the guitar amplifier at the far left, beside the lead rather than behind a body. One amber instrument cable plugs visibly into the guitar's outward-facing lower-body jack, drops into a clear foreground strip to the left of both shoes, makes one broad U on the floor, then rises into the amplifier's visible input socket. Its entire uninterrupted route and both plugged endpoints are brightly separable from the dark floor. The bassist's small wireless transmitter keeps that floor strip clear while their own hands visibly fret and pluck the bass. At right, the compact drum kit opens sideways toward the camera. The drummer sits on a round stool whose seat is visibly beneath the hips, whose central post descends through an open gap, and whose splayed feet visibly meet the floor. The drummer's separate feet are supported, with the near foot on the kick pedal and the other flat beside it. Set the snare forward and left of the knees, leaving the stool support exposed on its right. The near hand's stick runs from its visible grip to a tip pressed against the central snare membrane, with a tiny dimple at that exact point; the far hand holds the other stick raised clear of the near arm. A restrained warm pool of stage light joins the performers against a dark brick back wall, while softer neutral fill keeps faces, hands, sockets, cable, snare skin and stool supports readable. A thin side fill makes the existing trouser folds and the hip-to-seat contact shadow legible at the stool edge. Keep enough stage floor and air around every support endpoint for this complete connected performance to fit comfortably inside one coherent photograph.
